scope: AIOC-only preimplementation contract closure; no Multiversal-app PCV runtime implementation, schema migration execution, networking activation, gameplay convergence or package/release mutation

application_sources: historical Multiversal-app PR #775 PCV-03 session/runtime candidate

core_invariants.one_history: Campaign/Session/Action/Event durable truth remains one ordered history across local-host, future hosted, live, async and hybrid execution. Transport/profile/mode changes never fork Session ids, command/event ledgers or recovery authority.
core_invariants.one_executor: Exactly one current Session authority executor assigns authoritative command/event order for a Session authority epoch.
core_invariants.realtime_advisory: WebRTC/WebSocket delivery is advisory. A packet, ACK, presence update or connection state can never become canonical merely because it arrived first.
core_invariants.commands_are_intent: Commands are proposed intent; committed Events/owner-domain records are facts. Client timestamps, revision claims, transport ordering and device identity are inputs/context only.
core_invariants.hidden_before_publication: Viewer payloads are authorization-filtered before transport. Recovery metadata must not reveal hidden Event cardinality.

command_identity_and_idempotency.command_id: Immutable unique command-attempt/operation record identity. It is never reused for a different semantic request.
command_identity_and_idempotency.idempotency_key: Stable semantic-effect identity scoped at minimum by Session and owning operation type. A client reuses the same idempotencyKey after timeout/ambiguous delivery when it is asking whether the same intended effect committed.

payload_fingerprint.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme over the normalized semantic tuple
tuple: operation-specific authorization/version references that affect semantics
payload_fingerprint.rule: same idempotencyKey + same payloadFingerprint returns the durable prior receipt and emits no second authoritative effect; same idempotencyKey + different fingerprint is a conflict with zero mutation

command_identity_and_idempotency.duplicate_command_id_rule: A repeated commandId must resolve to the same idempotency key/fingerprint/receipt. Any mismatch is a protocol/integrity conflict, not a new command.
command_identity_and_idempotency.ambiguous_outcome_rule: After uncertain transport outcome, query durable operation/command status by stable identity before minting a new idempotency key.

host_time.client_submitted_at: advisory provenance only; may be retained as clientSubmittedAt after validation
host_time.occurred_at: host/executor commit/event time assigned inside the serialized authoritative operation
host_time.rule: client-supplied time never becomes authoritative Event occurredAt, presence lastSeenAt, credential lifecycle time or ordering source

command_identity_and_idempotency.pcv03_command_surface: PCV-03 runtime exposes only explicitly typed/allowlisted Session-continuity/proof commands owned by PCV-03. Unknown/arbitrary SessionCommand.type or payload is rejected. A5 pause/resume/close remains A5 SessionRepositoryPort; gameplay/action convergence remains PCV-04+ and cannot enter through a generic PCV-03 command escape hatch.

serialized_mutation_and_outbox.transaction_boundary: PCV-I02 PersistencePort.transaction over one canonical database transaction
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.per_session_serialization: Before assigning command_sequence, revision or Event sequence, lock/serialize the current Session authority row/stream for that Session. Transport ordered delivery is insufficient because asynchronous handlers may overlap.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.local_sqlite: Use one write transaction on the installed SQLite database. SQLite serializes writers; the application still owns per-Session semantic sequencing, idempotency checks and deterministic ordering inside the transaction.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.managed_postgres: Lock the current Session row/sequence allocator within the transaction (for example SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or equivalent adapter semantics) so competing writers cannot assign the same next revision/sequence or observe a half-applied command.
commit_order: load and lock current Session lifecycle/revision/authority epoch
revalidate current A3 subject/device, A5 membership/permissions, entitlement and operation-specific authorization
resolve existing idempotency key/command identity and compare payload fingerprint
assign next commandSequence and canonical host receipt time
apply all owner-domain state deltas atomically
append immutable Event(s) with contiguous global eventSequence, causation/correlation and host occurredAt
insert transactional outbox record(s) with deterministic dedup keys
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.rollback_rule: Any validation, authorization, stale version, fingerprint conflict, domain mutation, Event append, checkpoint or outbox failure rolls back the authoritative operation.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.outbox_rule: Realtime dispatch occurs only after commit. The local-host SQLite profile and future PostgreSQL profile both use durable outbox/event-sequence semantics; delivery failure retries/advises from durable records and cannot roll back or recreate the committed Event.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.local_direct_mapping: Zero-service WebRTC dispatcher drains committed local outbox items or reads committed Event/projection records and pushes advisory frames. It never sends an authoritative-success frame before durable commit.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.hosted_mapping: SMB-01 Postgres transactional outbox feeds advisory realtime/WebSocket adapters with identical semantic receipts.
serialized_mutation_and_outbox.crash_rule: After executor restart, pending/uncertain outbox rows and durable command receipts are resumed idempotently; committed domain/Event history is not re-applied.

launched.join: allowed only after current authorization/policy/capability checks
launched.reconnect: allowed after current authorization and recovery validation
launched.continuity_commands: allowed if explicitly owned and typed

paused.new_mutating_commands: denied except the explicit A5 lifecycle transition that resumes/closes the Session
paused.reconnect: may restore an authorized read/recovery projection of the paused Session but grants no mutation authority until A5 status becomes launched
paused.presence: advisory connection presence may exist but cannot imply playable/mutating status

closed.credentials: all Session-scoped invitations, resume/rendezvous credentials and peer bindings revoked or rendered unusable
closed.historical_read: only through normal owner/visibility policy over durable history

session_lifecycle_and_authority_epoch.active_pointer_rule: A UI/local `active-host` pointer is a convenience projection only. Addressing an old Session id never bypasses its canonical A5 status.
session_lifecycle_and_authority_epoch.replacement_rule: Launching a new Session does not silently mutate unrelated Sessions. A UX flow that replaces/supersedes a current Session must explicitly close/handoff the old canonical Session (or use a future atomic replacement operation) and revoke its Session-scoped credentials before treating the replacement as current.

increments_on: authoritative executor handoff/migration for the same Session
recovery event that deliberately establishes a new authority generation after verified checkpoint/history restoration
authority_epoch.stale_epoch: commands, resume credentials, peer bindings and recovery claims bound to an older epoch fail closed
authority_epoch.handoff_commit: epoch transition is a durable audited Session operation and commits checkpoint/handoff evidence plus credential revocation/reissue metadata atomically

authoritative_stream.rule: Every committed Event receives one contiguous monotonically increasing sequence from the current authority executor. Sequence is assigned only inside the serialized commit.

viewer_projection_stream.reason: A player-visible list can legitimately omit hidden global Events, so global sequence gaps cannot be used as player loss detection and exposing them can leak hidden cardinality.
viewer_projection_stream.identity: viewerProjectionStreamId = Session + canonical viewer subject + projection policy/authorization epoch
viewer_projection_stream.server_internal_source_cursor: sourceEventSequenceProcessed; may advance across hidden Events without being exposed as hidden cardinality
viewer_projection_stream.public_delivery_cursor: projectionSequence; contiguous only over frames/events actually emitted to that viewer stream
viewer_projection_stream.reset_rule: Material visibility/role/permissions changes create a new projection stream epoch or force an authorized snapshot/resync before further incremental delivery.

delivery_batch: projection items with opaque source Event references where permitted

ack_semantics.rule: ACK means the receiver validated and applied the specific authorized projection batch to its recovery state. A join-accepted message, command receipt or host lastSequence is never an ACK.
ack_semantics.advancement: Client durable/locally recoverable projection cursor advances only after successful batch application. Host per-device ACK cursor advances only after receiving a valid ACK bound to batch/stream/fingerprint.
ack_semantics.forbidden: Do not copy authoritative global lastSequence into lastAcknowledgedSequence before delivery.
ack_semantics.lost_ack: Redelivery from the prior ACK cursor is safe; duplicate projection items are suppressed by stream/batch/event identity.

authoritative_event_and_viewer_delivery.gap_detection: The client detects loss by contiguous projectionSequence within its viewer stream. The authority detects replay/source continuity using internal globalEventSequence. Hidden global Events therefore do not look like loss, and actual missing visible delivery cannot be mistaken for secrecy.
authoritative_event_and_viewer_delivery.recovery_query: Reconnect requests the last durable viewer ACK cursor/stream epoch; host revalidates authorization, advances its internal source cursor through hidden Events, and emits only currently authorized projection items.

checkpoint_digest.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS over canonical checkpoint contents excluding digest/fingerprint fields
checkpoint_digest.verification: Recompute from loaded content and compare to a trusted digest/reference obtained from canonical checkpoint metadata or a verified backup/archive manifest; never compare a value only to itself from the same untrusted payload.

replay_fingerprint.definition: JCS hash over {sessionId, authorityEpoch, checkpointRevision, checkpointLastGlobalEventSequence, checkpointDigest, ordered replay Event identities/sequences/revisions/types/content digests, resultingRevision, resultingLastGlobalEventSequence}
replay_fingerprint.purpose: Binds the exact trusted checkpoint plus exact ordered tail used to reconstruct the resulting Session state/history.
replay_fingerprint.lifecycle: Compute for every validated restore/reconnect replay target and persist/reference it in recovery evidence; recompute after additional tail Events before claiming an equivalent recovery point.

checkpoint_and_replay_integrity.event_content_digest: Runtime implementation adds/derives a stable SHA-256 JCS content digest for each replayed canonical Event or equivalent trusted immutable-event digest so replayFingerprint is not only a list of labels.

required_points: graceful pause/close where a current recovery point is useful
checkpoint_roll_forward.periodic_policy: A versioned recovery policy may checkpoint after a bounded Event count and/or maximum age. Thresholds are configuration/policy, not scattered magic constants.
checkpoint_roll_forward.rule: Checkpoint creation never changes Event history; a checkpoint is a verified acceleration/recovery snapshot of one exact revision/sequence.

checkpoint_and_replay_integrity.restore_rule: Restore verifies Session id, trusted checkpoint digest, schema compatibility, authority epoch/handoff evidence and contiguous canonical Event replay. Any digest, sequence, revision, schema or authorization mismatch fails closed/quarantines recovery.
checkpoint_and_replay_integrity.backup_rule: A restored backup does not silently resume old credentials or authority. After verified history restoration, current authorization is rechecked and a deliberate new authority epoch is established when the restored executor becomes authoritative.

current_authorization_required: current A3 StableSubjectSession and PCV-I01A device proof
current A5 membership active/unexpired and membershipVersion
Session lifecycle permits the requested recovery mode
resume/rendezvous credential is current and bound to current Session/subject/device/authorityEpoch
reconnect_and_rendezvous.caller_state_rule: Caller-supplied revision, lastSequence, role, membershipActive, permissionCurrent, checkpoint checksum or authorityEpoch is never trusted as proof; it is at most a requested cursor/hint checked against canonical state.
reconnect_and_rendezvous.invitation_separation: An already-authorized member does not need a new Campaign membership invitation merely to establish a replacement transport. Invitation acceptance and reconnect rendezvous are separate operations.
reconnect_and_rendezvous.reconnect_rendezvous: PCV runtime supplies a short-lived single-use reconnect/rendezvous credential or equivalent authenticated signaling flow scoped to existing Session membership/device continuity. It grants transport establishment only and cannot mint membership/role.
reconnect_and_rendezvous.resume_rotation: Successful reconnect rotates/reissues Session resume/rendezvous bearer material as policy requires; stale/used credentials are revoked. Raw bearer handling follows PCV-I02/I03 secret/no-log rules.
recovery_order: select and verify trusted checkpoint/replay target
restore or confirm canonical Session state
resume viewer projection from durable viewer ACK cursor
only then enable owned mutating command surface when Session is launched

presence_projection.authority: none; presence is advisory session UI state
presence_projection.identity_source: current PCV-I03 PeerAuthorizationBinding supplies subjectId/deviceId/transportInstanceId; presence payload cannot choose them
presence_projection.time_source: authority executor receipt/connection lifecycle time; client timestamp is ignored for durable/advisory lastSeenAt
presence_projection.connected: derived after authenticated peer binding is established and application channel is authorized
presence_projection.idle: derived by host policy from bounded inactivity; does not revoke membership
presence_projection.reconnecting: bounded transient host projection after connection loss when current Session/reconnect policy permits
presence_projection.disconnected: derived immediately from trusted DataChannel/transport close/failure or reconnect timeout; client does not need to send a final message
presence_projection.heartbeat: If used, heartbeat carries no identity/role authority; receipt only refreshes the already-bound transport's host-side lastSeenAt.
presence_projection.persistence: May retain bounded non-authoritative diagnostics/last-seen metadata, but presence is not Campaign membership, device identity, Session lifecycle or Event truth and is excluded from canonical replay requirements.

hybrid_live_async_continuity.identity: CampaignId and SessionId remain unchanged while a Session moves between live, async and hybrid interaction cadence.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.history: All accepted async and live authoritative operations enter the same serialized Session command/Event history and monotonically advance the same revision/global Event sequence.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.disconnect_rule: Going offline/disconnected changes presence only. It does not fork/copy the Session or grant broad offline authoritative mutation.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.async_resolution: GM/owner-domain async resolution commits through the same canonical authority executor/PersistencePort transaction and is visible to returning clients only through authorized recovery projection.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.return_to_live: On return, revalidate current authorization, restore/confirm checkpoint + ordered tail, recover missed visible projection items from the durable viewer ACK cursor, then resume live transport on the same Session history.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.at_most_once_effect: Stable idempotencyKey + payloadFingerprint ensures a retry/reconnect cannot create a second accepted Action/effect; status lookup returns the first durable result.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.profile_handoff: Local-host and future hosted executors use the same Session ids, epoch, command/event sequence, checkpoint/replay and viewer-cursor semantics. Profile handoff is an authority-epoch transition over verified same-history evidence, not data import into a new ledger.
hybrid_live_async_continuity.apw_compatibility: Preserves APW-I07 live-before -> async-submitted -> disconnected -> gm-resolved -> player-returned -> live-resumed contract: the returned live cursor reflects the one committed async result, recovered missed Event evidence and no second Campaign ledger.

logical_schema_runtime_delta.owner: PCV runtime implementation under later authorized tranche; PCV-I04 freezes semantics but does not execute migration
session_commands_additive: resulting_revision/receipt_reference or equivalent durable receipt binding
session_events_additive: revision if not otherwise durably derivable
logical_schema_runtime_delta.recovery_metadata: Durable viewer projection stream/cursor/ACK records from PCV-I02 classification: sourceEventSequenceProcessed internal, projectionSequence issued/acked, stream epoch/policy version, subject/device/session binding and replay fingerprint.
logical_schema_runtime_delta.outbox: Existing outbox_events remains the durable post-commit delivery source; add stable Session/Event/projection dedup/reference metadata as needed rather than creating a second realtime ledger.
logical_schema_runtime_delta.migration_rule: Use additive reviewed migration(s) after revalidating the then-current migration registry; do not rewrite 0001 history.

external_sanity_checks.use: canonical JSON provides invariant hash input for payload, checkpoint and replay fingerprints
SQLite serializes writes and exposes only committed transactions across normal connections; local adapter still must serialize Session semantics inside one transaction
single local transaction provides atomic all-or-nothing durable state/Event/outbox commits
row-level FOR UPDATE-style locking can serialize competing managed-profile Session mutations until transaction end
ordered=true is the default transport delivery property, but application async handlers still require explicit authoritative mutation serialization

runtime_boundary.next_runtime_destination: PCV-03B/PCV-03D only after PCV-I05 through PCV-I06 predecessor closure
